message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the 2003 Mr. Basketball USA and the 2004 Naismith High School Player of the Year.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). He has been selected to the All‑NBA First Team 18 times and has been named an NBA All‑Star 19 times (as of 2023).

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at-risk children. He is also a media entrepreneur, producing and starring in films and television series, and has a significant presence in endorsements and business ventures.

In short, LeBron James is a basketball superstar, cultural icon, philanthropist, and entrepreneur whose impact extends far beyond the sport.
